Industrial robots

Renesas launches RZ/T2N for four-axis control and industrial networking

The MPU and evaluation board are available, while functional-safety software is planned for the second half of 2027.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗5 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

Consolidating industrial functions

Renesas introduced the 64-bit RZ/T2N MPU on November 5, combining real-time motor control, industrial Ethernet and application processing. It targets industrial robots, multi-axis servos and PLCs. Fewer chips could simplify boards, but the announcement gives no universal percentage saving in cost or footprint.

Different cores for different workloads

Two Cortex-A55 cores run at up to 1.2 GHz, alongside two Cortex-R52 cores at up to 800 MHz. Integrated peripherals support up to four motor axes. EtherCAT, PROFINET RT/IRT, EtherNet/IP and TSN support controller and device roles, with Linux handling application workloads.

Available hardware and future software

The MPU and evaluation board are available, with secure boot, secure firmware updates and Arm TrustZone. Functional-safety software solutions are planned for the second half of 2027. Developers must distinguish currently available hardware from that roadmap and assess the safety requirements of their complete system.
